HOUSEHOLD AIeverything i built ↗

ever wanted to automate something, privacy first?

Well, I did exactly that. For meetings, at least.

Built with Fathom, n8n, an AI model running on my own computer, Notion and Google Calendar. Never heard of some of these? Each one gets a one-line intro below.

source code ↗
HOW IT WORKS
ONLINEON YOUR COMPUTER

How it works

  1. 1

    Fathom records the meeting

    You set up Fathom so it joins your meetings and writes down everything said.

    Fathom is an AI note-taker. It sits in on your calls so you don’t have to scribble.

  2. meanwhile, online:
    nothing. steps 2 to 4
    never leave your computer.
  3. 2

    your computer picks it up

    n8n, running on your computer, fetches what Fathom wrote down.

    n8n is a very patient robot that follows a flowchart: when this happens, do that, then that.

  4. 3

    AI turns it into to-dos

    An AI model on your own computer turns the meeting into points you can act on. Personal details, like a CNIC or a card number, are stripped out.

    Same idea as ChatGPT, just smaller, and it runs on my graphics card instead of someone else’s servers.

  5. 4

    you say yes or no

    You review those points, then accept or reject them. Nothing is saved anywhere until you do.

  6. 5

    Notion and your calendar get updated

    The points go into a Notion page, and any plans you made land on your calendar.

    Notion is a notebook that lives online and syncs to your phone.

6

and for the paperwork

Drowning in documents? Put them in a folder, ask a question, and the AI answers from those papers and tells you which one it used. No digging through all of them, and nothing leaves your computer.

One honest catch: Fathom itself hears the meeting. Everything after that stays on your computer.

DOES IT WORK?

Does it work?

20 of 21questions about a pile of test documents answered correctly
under 30 sto turn a meeting into to-dos, on my own graphics card
0duplicates, even when the same meeting came in twice
55automatic checks that run every time I change the code
WHAT I LEARNED BUILDING IT

What I learned building it

  • Small AI models are bad at dates. It kept putting “tomorrow” on the day of the meeting, so now the AI only notes the words and the code works out the date.
  • Computers wake up before the Wi-Fi does. Right after a restart, saving to Notion failed. Now it waits for the internet first.
  • It lives on my PC. When my PC is off, so is this. A version that runs online is next.
